labels.label: Nominal tokens vs function/punctuation tokens
labels.description: Positive activations tend to mark nouns or pronouns (e.g., 'garden', 'oil'); negative activations mark determiners, auxiliaries, or punctuation (e.g., 'the', 'did'). The contrast appears across documents and within 'how we did'.
Positive and negative examples mix word-initial fragments, word-final suffixes, URL punctuation, names, and common words; no stable recurrent token or context pattern is supported.
Positive and negative examples mix common words, name/place prefixes, punctuation, digits, and suffixes across unrelated contexts; no stable recurrent pattern is supported.

labels.label: Lowercase common words vs proper-name tokens
labels.description: Positive activations are mostly lower-case common words or URL text (e.g., 'the', 'important'); negative activations concentrate on capitalized proper-name/nationality tokens (e.g., 'German', 'Italian').
labels.positive: Lower-case common words such as 'the' and 'important'.
labels.negative: Capitalized proper-name/nationality tokens such as 'German' and 'Italian'.
